issues.description: The problem statement requires calculateTotalPrice to be a static method (see note lines stating it must be static), but the reference solution implements calculateTotalPrice as an instance method (non-static). This mismatch between the specification and the solution can confuse students about whether the method should be static and may cause integration issues if tests or instructions expect static usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Align implementation and specification: either make calculateTotalPrice static in the solution and template (e.g., public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal)) and update any callers accordingly, or update the problem statement to remove the requirement that calculateTotalPrice be static so the instance method in the solution matches the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement contains an internal contradiction about the static nature of members: the UML fragment does not mark calculateTotalPrice as static, while the textual instructions explicitly require calculateTotalPrice (and stock and acceptSupplyDelivery) to be static. This inconsistency between the UML diagram and the written requirements may confuse students about the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement so the UML and textual instructions agree. Either update the UML to explicitly indicate the static members (e.g., underline or stereotype) or remove the textual requirement for calculateTotalPrice to be static. Make a single, consistent statement about which attributes/methods should be static.
